question: Which virus is the main cause of cervical cancer?
explanation: Persistent infection with high-risk strains of the Human Papillomavirus causes cellular changes that lead to cervical cancer. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T18#GNS216_U5_T18_h1)

question: Why is the transformation zone of the cervix most at risk for abnormal cell changes?

options.A: It is constantly exposed to seminal fluid during sex.
options.B: Active cell changes make it vulnerable to viral damage.
options.C: It produces thick mucus that traps bacteria.
options.D: It contains the most nerve endings in the reproductive tract.

explanation: Continuous cell changes and tissue remodeling in the transformation zone make these cells prone to HPV infection and abnormal growth. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T18#GNS216_U5_T18_h1)

question: Why does a weakened immune system increase the risk of cervical cancer?

options.A: It increases protective cervical mucus production.
options.B: It makes the body more sensitive to anti-inflammatory drugs.
options.C: It prevents the body from clearing ongoing HPV infections.
options.D: It directly speeds up tumor cell division.

explanation: Immunosuppressed individuals, such as those with untreated HIV, struggle to fight off and clear initial HPV infections. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T18#GNS216_U5_T18_h2)

question: How does cigarette smoking contribute to cervical cancer?

options.A: By depositing tobacco chemicals directly into cervical secretions
options.B: By speeding up the onset of menopause
options.C: By changing vaginal pH to favor bad bacteria
options.D: By causing vitamin deficiencies that weaken pelvic muscles

explanation: Harmful chemicals from cigarette smoke end up in cervical mucus, where they directly damage the DNA of local cells. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T18#GNS216_U5_T18_h2)

question: What is the most common early sign of cervical cancer?
explanation: Bleeding after sex happens because early tumor tissue on the cervix is fragile and easily irritated. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T18#GNS216_U5_T18_h3)

question: Why might a patient with advanced cervical cancer feel severe pain shooting down her legs?

options.B: Muscle spasms from pelvic inflammatory disease
options.C: Cancer spreading into the bones of the lower limbs
options.D: The tumor pressing on nerves in the pelvis

explanation: As the tumor grows and spreads outward, it can press on nearby pelvic nerves, causing radiating pain. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T18#GNS216_U5_T18_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of a colposcopy?

options.A: To magnify and closely check abnormal areas of the cervix using special solutions
options.B: To measure hormone levels in the blood
options.C: To check if the fallopian tubes are open
options.D: To destroy abnormal cells using freezing probes

explanation: A colposcope magnifies the cervix, and special liquids like vinegar help highlight abnormal tissue so doctors can take targeted tissue samples. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T18#GNS216_U5_T18_h4)

question: Why is a routine Pap smear considered secondary prevention rather than primary prevention?

options.A: It finds existing cell changes rather than stopping the initial infection.
options.B: It only works for women who have finished having children.
options.C: It relies on surgery instead of health education.
options.D: It can only be done after a confirmed cancer diagnosis.

explanation: Screening tests catch disease early when it is treatable, whereas primary prevention stops the disease from happening in the first place. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T18#GNS216_U5_T18_h4)

question: What is the standard treatment for locally advanced cervical cancer?

options.B: Surgery to remove the entire uterus alone

explanation: Locally advanced cervical cancer is best treated with a combination of systemic drugs and targeted radiation to destroy the cancer cells. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T18#GNS216_U5_T18_h5)

question: Why is a radioactive source placed directly into the vagina for short periods during brachytherapy?

options.A: To block the growth of new blood vessels feeding the cancer
options.B: To stimulate the immune system to fight remaining cancer cells
options.C: To clean the vagina and prevent bacterial infections
options.D: To deliver a high dose of radiation to the tumor while protecting healthy tissues nearby

explanation: Brachytherapy delivers targeted internal radiation, maximizing cancer destruction while keeping nearby organs like the bladder safe. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T18#GNS216_U5_T18_h5)

question: What is a major care priority after a patient undergoes a radical hysterectomy?

options.A: Checking for bleeding in the lungs
options.B: Assessing for bladder problems and inability to pass urine
options.C: Monitoring for sudden high blood sugar

explanation: A radical hysterectomy often disturbs the pelvic nerves that control the bladder, making it hard for the patient to urinate afterward. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T18#GNS216_U5_T18_h6)

question: Why is emotional support an important part of nursing care for cervical cancer patients?

options.A: The diagnosis often deeply affects body image, sexuality, and fertility.
options.B: Positive attitudes stop patients from having side effects.
options.C: Counseling completely replaces the need for surgery.
options.D: Emotional stress stops chemotherapy drugs from working.

explanation: Because cervical cancer involves reproductive organs, treatment often causes significant emotional distress regarding body image and childbearing. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T18#GNS216_U5_T18_h6)

question: Who is the main target group for the HPV vaccine?

options.A: Adult men with sexually transmitted infections
options.C: Young adolescent girls before they become sexually active

explanation: HPV vaccines work best when given before a person is exposed to the virus through sexual activity. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T18#GNS216_U5_T18_h7)

question: Why is Visual Inspection with Acetic Acid (VIA) useful in low-resource clinics in Nigeria?

options.A: It removes the need for any future medical checkups.
options.B: It uses radiation to destroy abnormal cells instantly.
options.C: It is the only test that can stage advanced cancers.
options.D: It gives immediate results without needing complex laboratory equipment.

explanation: VIA allows nurses to check the cervix and see results right away, making it easy to treat patients on the spot where lab facilities are missing. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T18#GNS216_U5_T18_h7)
